posts.title: How to Reduce Food Waste at Home
posts.excerpt: Simple habits to track expiry dates, organize your fridge, and save money every week.
posts.content:
Simple habits to track expiry dates, organize your fridge, and save money every week.

Start by auditing what you throw away for one week. Write down every item that goes in the bin — you'll see patterns quickly.

Then set up a system: zone your fridge, label leftovers with dates, and plan meals around what's already in stock before buying more.

Use an app like FreshGuard to get reminders before items expire, so nothing gets forgotten at the back of the fridge.

posts.title: Use By vs Best Before: What the Dates Really Mean
posts.excerpt: Understanding food date labels to stop throwing away good food.
posts.content:
"Use by" is about safety. After this date, food may be unsafe to eat.

"Best before" is about quality. The food might not taste as fresh, but it's usually still safe if stored properly.

FreshGuard lets you choose which type each item has — you're always in control.

Most food waste happens because people confuse these two labels and throw away perfectly good food.

posts.title: FIFO Kitchen Organization: First In, First Out
posts.excerpt: Zone-based storage and rotation to keep produce fresh longer.
posts.content:
FIFO (First In, First Out) means newer items go to the back, older items to the front.

When you unpack groceries, move older products forward so they get used first. Apply this to your fridge, freezer, and pantry.

Combine FIFO with FreshGuard's location-based inventory to see exactly what you have and where.

posts.title: Meal Planning to Reduce Food Waste
posts.excerpt: Plan your meals around what you already have to save money and reduce waste.
posts.content:
Meal planning is one of the most effective ways to reduce food waste.

Start by checking what's in your fridge, freezer, and pantry — use FreshGuard to see your inventory at a glance.

Plan meals that use up items closest to expiry first. Build your shopping list only for what's missing.

This simple habit can reduce household food waste by up to 30%.

posts.title: Planification des repas pour réduire le gaspillage
posts.excerpt: Planifiez vos repas autour de ce que vous avez déjà pour économiser et réduire le gaspillage.
posts.content:
La planification des repas est l'un des moyens les plus efficaces pour réduire le gaspillage alimentaire.

Commencez par vérifier ce qui se trouve dans votre réfrigérateur, congélateur et garde-manger — utilisez FreshGuard pour voir votre inventaire d'un coup d'œil.

Planifiez les repas qui utilisent les produits dont la date approche en premier. Faites votre liste de courses uniquement pour ce qui manque.

Cette habitude simple peut réduire le gaspillage alimentaire de votre foyer jusqu'à 30%.

posts.title: Digital Minimalism: Reclaim Your Attention
posts.excerpt: How to use your phone intentionally and reduce digital distraction.
posts.content:
Digital minimalism means using technology with intention, not habit.

Audit your apps weekly. Delete what you don't use. Turn off non-essential notifications.

Batch-check email and messages instead of responding to every ping immediately.

Your attention is your most valuable resource — protect it.

posts.title: Minimalisme numérique : reprendre le contrôle
posts.excerpt: Comment utiliser votre téléphone de manière intentionnelle et réduire la distraction numérique.
posts.content:

posts.excerpt: How cookies work, what AdSense uses them for, and how to opt out.
posts.content:

When AdSense is enabled on SmartLife Hub, Google may use advertising cookies to show relevant ads. You can opt out anytime via Google Ads Settings.
